ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian ـدار (-dār). Compare Bengali -দার (-dar), Punjabi -ਦਾਰ (-dār).

s.g: instructor, director, one who governs or punishes

ety.text: Learned borrowing from Sanskrit अनुशासक (anuśāsaka). By surface analysis, अनु- (anu-) + शासक (śāsak).

x: दुसरों को देखने से पहले अपना ख़्याल रखो।

ety.text: Inherited from Old Hindi अपना (apanā), आपन (āpana), आपना (āpanā), from Prakrit अप्पणय (appaṇaya, “own”), from Sanskrit *आत्मनक (*ātmanaka). The Prakrit form is based on अप्पण (appaṇa, “self”) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓- (-ka-) and replaces Sanskrit आत्मक (ātmaka, “belong to”), for which compare Hindi -आत्मक (-ātmak). Cognate with Gujarati આપણું (āpaṇũ), Punjabi ਆਪਣਾ (āpaṇā), Nepali आफ्नो (āphno), and Bengali আপন (apon). Related to आप (āp, “you, self”).
Learned borrowing from Sanskrit अवकल (avakala, “subtraction, difference”).

s.g: Alambagh (a neighbourhood of Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India)

x: मंडी में छोटी सी बात पर दो लोगों के बीच कहासुनी हो गई।

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian غَنِیمَت (ġanīmat), from Arabic غَنِيمَة (ḡanīma).

s.g: partly dyed (usually red) cloth (of which portions have escaped the dyeing process by being twisted or knotted together)
the process of dyeing cunrī cloth

ety.text: Compare Punjabi ਚੁੰਨੀ (cunnī). Derived from Sanskrit [Term?].
Borrowed from Sikkimese ཆོས་རྒྱལ (chos rgyal), a calque of Sanskrit धर्मराज (dharmarāja, “dharma king”).

s.g: Zagreb (the capital and largest city of Croatia)
To make a muscle, to flex one's arm muscles proudly.

ety.text: Vagish Shastri derives the word from Sanskrit पल्पूल (palpūla), related to the root प्लु (plu, “to float, swim; to hop, leap, jump”). Cognate with Bundeli पपोरबौ (paporbau). Related to परोरना (parornā, “to consecrate, to incantate, to breathe a spell”).

s.g: unit of time equalling three hours
to become extremely afraid, scared or frightened
